name: Heist / Caper
definition: A skilled group attempts a difficult theft whose pleasure comes from expertise, coordination, misdirection, and adaptation under pressure.
diagnostic_questions: Is the method of taking the target a central source of reader pleasure?
Does success depend on complementary skills or coordinated roles?

neighbors.distinction: A heist enters a protected system to take something; an escape exits confinement.
A heist foregrounds an operation, while conspiracy foregrounds hidden power and discovery.

reader_promises.name: The impossible job
reader_promises.description: Present a target and security problem whose difficulty invites strategic curiosity.

reader_promises.name: Competence under pressure
reader_promises.description: Let specialized skills matter while human limits make flawless execution impossible.

reader_promises.name: Earned misdirection
reader_promises.description: Withhold or redirect information without invalidating what the reader has observed.

roles.name: Architect
roles.description: Defines the objective and integrates the operation into one workable concept.

roles.name: Specialist
roles.description: Solves a distinctive technical, social, physical, or logistical barrier.

roles.name: Wildcard
roles.description: Adds an unstable loyalty, unusual method, or pressure the plan cannot fully absorb.

movements.name: Proposition
movements.description: Establish the target, motive, constraints, and reason this attempt matters now.

movements.name: Reconnaissance
movements.description: Discover useful vulnerabilities while exposing gaps, costs, or false assumptions.

movements.name: Operation
movements.description: Put coordinated choices into motion and make each success create a new exposure.

movements.name: Aftermath
movements.description: Resolve possession, pursuit, loyalty, and the personal meaning of success or failure.

complications.name: Security change
complications.description: A rule, guard pattern, or physical condition changes after planning.

complications.name: Human fracture
complications.description: Fear, pride, affection, or conflicting need disrupts coordination.

complications.name: Third party
complications.description: A rival, investigator, or opportunist enters the operation with a separate goal.

twists.name: Hidden operational layer
twists.description: An earlier detail gains a second function that was fairly prepared.

twists.name: Target redefined
twists.description: The apparent prize conceals different value, ownership, or moral consequence.

conclusions.name: Clean win
conclusions.description: The crew secures the true objective and exits through earned coordination.

conclusions.name: Costly win
conclusions.description: The objective is gained while trust, freedom, or identity is irreversibly lost.

conclusions.name: Productive failure
conclusions.description: The theft fails but exposes corruption, saves someone, or changes the crew's purpose.

variation_axes.question: Why is the job worth the risk?
How much of the plan does the reader know?

subversions: Let a small personal objective matter more than the advertised prize.
Make empathy and social perception more decisive than technology.
cliches_to_avoid: A specialist whose only trait is a job label
A twist that depends on information the story dishonestly erased
quality_checks: Every displayed skill changes an obstacle or consequence.
Complications arise from security, character, or prior choices rather than coincidence.
The aftermath resolves both the objective and the crew's relationships.

sources.title: The Heist
sources.contribution: Identifies planning, execution, and aftermath as recurring heist stages.

sources.title: The Team Film Genre
sources.contribution: Analyzes team assembly, differentiated skills, preparation, main operation, and coda.
